HSBC cut LVMH to hold from its previous rating, with a price target of €490. HSBC also cut Burberry to hold, setting a price target of 1,200 pence.

The bank's more cautious stance reflects softer momentum across the luxury sector, with HSBC highlighting near-term challenges in soft luxury and muted trends that could limit investor appetite for the sector.

According to reports, the brokerage noted slower than expected performance at Dior alongside the weaker Fashion and Leather Goods division. The firm maintains confidence in the division’s mid-to-long term growth potential but is moving to the sidelines given the current macro environment.
On a YTD basis, LVMH ADRs down 35%, BURBY slipped 15%.

title: HSBC warns of tough H2 for European luxury stocks, downgrades LVMH, Burberry
